# SUI-19 — Title Case preset labels and neutral preset hints

**Tracking issue:** https://github.com/tonygward/audio-plugins/issues/266
**Origin:** Generated by Matrix from the tracking issue when the card was picked up, because no prompt file existed and the issue had enough detail. The issue text below is the specification.

## Objective
Bring the factory preset text that predates the CLAUDE.md naming rule into line with it: names in Title Case that describe the use, and no personal or album provenance in on-screen help.

## Scope
- **Songsmith Analog Compressor** starting points show sentence case in the Preset menu: "Lead vocal", "Acoustic guitar", "Bass", "Drum room". Give them Title Case use-case labels (for example "Lead Vocal Control", "Acoustic Guitar", "Bass Guitar", "Drum Room").
- **Songsmith Maximiser** starting points: "Mix bus", "Demo loudness", "Final export" become Title Case labels (for example "Mix Bus", "Demo Loudness", "Final Export").
- **Songsmith EQ:** the menu labels already follow the rule since EQ-40 ("Effects - Reverb Send Clean-up", "Drums - Floor Tom"); no renaming. The tom hints say "Tony's ... EQ from Between You and Me" on screen. Rewrite them in plain operational language and keep the provenance in `eq/docs/starting-points.md` (SUI-14).
- Display labels only: stored names, preset indices, program numbers and saved sessions keep working. User presets cannot clash with the new labels (the existing factory-name protection covers the new spellings).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every factory preset label in all three plugins is Title Case, describes its use, and passes the wording check.
- No on-screen hint names a person or an album.
- Older sessions and user presets load unchanged; the changelog explains the new labels in plain words.

## Tests
- Preset-label rule test over every factory list (Title Case, no banned words, no person or album names in hints).
- Recall tests for sessions and presets saved with the old names; factory-name protection still refuses the old and new spellings.
